title: LVM, capacity, and swap
subtitle: Build a flexible storage stack from physical volumes, volume groups, and logical volumes — then grow it without downtime.
objectives: Explain the PV, VG, and LV layers
Create a physical volume and volume group
Create a logical volume, format it, and mount it
Extend a logical volume and its XFS filesystem online
Plan swap and capacity with the right constraints

ex200.evidence: Read pvs, vgs, lvs, and lsblk as one stack.
pvcreate and vgcreate on a dedicated device.

versionNotes: The LVM command family is unchanged between RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 for this workflow; RHEL 10 uses the same device-mapper stack.
RHEL 9 and 10 both support online XFS growth. Shrinking XFS is not supported on either release.

sections.title: Create and mount a logical volume

commands.cmd: sudo pvs && sudo vgs && sudo lvs
commands.desc: Inspect all three LVM layers at once.
Initialise a block device as an LVM physical volume.
Create a volume group from one or more PVs.
Create a 5 GiB logical volume in vgdata.
Put an XFS filesystem on the logical volume.
Extend the LV and grow XFS in one operation.
Show physical-volume allocation and free extents.

lab.title: Build a volume group from a spare disk
lab.scenario: Use /dev/sdb in the sandbox as a spare disk. Create a PV, VG, LV, filesystem, and mount, then extend it. Finish by activating swap on /dev/sdc.

steps.text: Inspect the current LVM stack and confirm /dev/sdb is unused.
steps.cmd: lsblk && sudo pvs && sudo vgs && sudo lvs
steps.verify: /dev/sdb appears as a disk but not as a PV, VG, or LV.

steps.text: Initialise /dev/sdb as a physical volume and create vgdata.
steps.verify: pvs shows /dev/sdb in vgdata and vgs shows vgdata with free space.

steps.text: Create a 5 GiB logical volume named lvapp.
steps.cmd: sudo lvcreate -n lvapp -L 5G vgdata && sudo lvs
steps.verify: lvs lists vgdata/lvapp with the expected size.

steps.text: Format the LV with XFS, mount it at /app, and verify the mount.
steps.cmd: sudo mkfs.xfs /dev/vgdata/lvapp && sudo mkdir -p /app && sudo mount /dev/vgdata/lvapp /app && findmnt /app

steps.text: Extend the logical volume by 2 GiB and resize XFS in the same command.
steps.verify: The LV size and the mounted filesystem both grow; no unmount is required.

quiz.q: Which layer pools physical storage so logical volumes can be carved from it?
quiz.why: A volume group pools one or more physical volumes and allocates extents to logical volumes.

options: Resizes the filesystem after extending the volume
quiz.why: -r invokes the appropriate filesystem resize helper after extending the logical volume.

quiz.q: Which filesystem resize is supported online for XFS?
quiz.why: XFS supports online growth. Shrinking requires creating a new filesystem and migrating data.
